title: Power Pages: environment-level governance of external authentication providers
summary: Hold: the open questions present existing-site enforcement and coverage of Microsoft Entra External ID and local authentication as unsettled, although the cited documentation answers them. Both admin paths also omit the documented Products grouping. The roadmap metadata and the restriction control's opt-in default are supported.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Power Pages authentication-provider governance.
claims.quote: Power Pages: Administration and governance - Manage external authentication providers with granular controls

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans environment-level controls over the external authentication providers Power Pages makers may configure.
claims.quote: You can centrally enforce which identity providers (IDPs) are allowed across all sites in an environment

claims.claim: The planned environment-level controls support optional site-level exceptions.
claims.quote: environment-level governance controls and optional site-level exceptions

claims.claim: The roadmap says makers will only see and select approved identity providers when configuring authentication.
claims.quote: Makers will only see and select from the approved IDPs when setting up authentication

claims.claim: The roadmap item remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists January CY2027 as the general availability target.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"
claims.fix: After the roadmap dates, add: 'A separate Microsoft release-plan page lists January 2026; the roadmap currently targets January CY2027.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-pages/manage-external-authentication-provider-governance, whose availability table says 'Users, automatically | - | Jan 2026'.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists November CY2026 for preview.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap was modified at 2026-10-23T22:45:54.
The roadmap gives Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers.
claims.quote: To enable this feature, go to the Power Platform admin center. Navigate to Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers.

claims.claim: The roadmap says Enabled for end users automatically rather than specifying a default restriction.
claims.quote:
Enabled for:

claims.claim: The restriction control is admin-opt-in: all authentication options are allowed by default until an administrator configures restrictions.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure. No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.

claims.claim: Learn documents that a blocked protocol or provider appears dimmed in the design studio and cannot be configured.
claims.quote: In the design studio, a protocol or identity provider that governance blocks appears dimmed and can't be configured.

claims.claim: Previously configured tenant external-authentication restrictions are preserved and Microsoft advises reviewing them per environment.
claims.quote: If you set an external-authentication control for your tenant before environment-level granular governance was introduced, that setting is preserved. Review it for each environment to confirm that it still matches your intent.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The current authentication-governance path is Manage > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > option > environment > Manage.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Manage.
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Under Authentication, select the authentication option you want to manage.
Select an environment, and then select Manage.
claims.fix: Insert the documented Products grouping: 'Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > option > environment > Manage'. Apply this to controls[0].ui.path and both rendered and prose versions of the current Learn path.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the environment-level authentication-governance setting is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance Power Platform API, pac admin, PowerShell, Dataverse; targeted programmability, CLI, PowerShell and Dataverse searches. Opened external-auth-control and pac pages/admin references; no equivalent governance operation found.

claims.claim: Authentication-governance targeting supports all sites, all sites except selected sites, specific sites, and no sites in the environment.
claims.quote:
All sites in this environment
All sites except specific sites
Specific sites
None of the sites in this environment

claims.claim: Non-production public-access governance is at Manage > Power Pages > Settings > Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites > environment.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Manage.
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Select Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.
Select the environment you want to manage.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered version with 'Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites > environment', including the documented Products grouping.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for environment-level non-production public-access governance is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages non-production site visibility governance API PowerShell Set-PowerAppTenantSettings; Power Pages site visibility governance API non-production. Opened site-visibility-governance and pac pages/admin; results' Set-TenantSettings controls role delegation, not this policy.

claims.claim: Public-visibility governance for non-production sites is configured for a selected environment.
claims.quote:
This governance control applies when either the site or its environment is non-production.
Select the environment you want to manage.

claims.claim: Tenant administrators configure non-production public-access governance.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can control whether makers can make a Power Pages site public when either the site or its environment is non-production.

claims.claim: The authentication-governance Learn page does not specify the exact administrator role required.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance admin role permissions. Opened external-auth-control in full: it addresses 'an admin' and gives configuration steps without naming a required role. Separate RBAC search results do not change what this cited page states.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing for the new authentication-governance control has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance licensing prerequisite; Power Pages licensing FAQ. Opened external-auth-control and Power Platform licensing FAQs, including Power Pages and security/governance sections; no licence specific to this control found.

claims.claim: Feature-specific metering for authentication governance has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance licensing metering. Opened external-auth-control and Power Platform licensing FAQs: product user/website/month meters are documented, but no meter for applying authentication-governance settings was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a Managed Environments dependency for this authentication-governance control.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance Managed Environments prerequisite. Opened external-auth-control and licensing FAQ security/governance section; read managed-environment licensing search excerpts. None states this control requires Managed Environments.

claims.claim: Makers can currently pick any supported provider for a site.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure. No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.
claims.fix: Narrow the sentence to the documented default: 'By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure.' The existing sentence reads as unconditional despite the restrictions documented elsewhere on this same page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Blocking an authentication option affects existing live sites and stops sign-in through that option.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.

claims.claim: Authentication governance takes precedence over a site's existing maker configuration.
claims.quote: If an existing site configuration uses a sign-in method associated with a blocked option, the governance setting takes precedence.

claims.where: Open questions: existing-site enforcement; Governance controls
claims.claim: Whether enforcement blocks existing sites remains an open question.
claims.quote: Governance controls: 'sites that already use it stop authenticating users through it'. Open questions: 'Is enforcement blocking for existing sites, or only for new configuration?'
claims.fix: Remove 'Is enforcement blocking for existing sites, or only for new configuration?' from Open questions. The existing Governance controls paragraph already gives the answer verified at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/external-auth-control.

claims.where: Open questions: Microsoft Entra External ID coverage
claims.claim: Whether the authentication-governance control covers Microsoft Entra External ID is not yet answered.
claims.quote: OpenID Connect | OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers, including Microsoft Entra External ID.
claims.fix: Remove the Microsoft Entra External ID portion of 'Does it cover Microsoft Entra External ID and local sign-in?' from Open questions; the cited Learn page explicitly includes it under the preview OpenID Connect control.

claims.claim: Whether the authentication-governance control covers local sign-in is not yet answered.
claims.quote: Local authentication determines whether makers can configure username and password sign-in by using locally stored accounts. It's available only when the site also allows external authentication.
claims.fix: Remove the local sign-in portion of 'Does it cover Microsoft Entra External ID and local sign-in?' from Open questions. Together with the External ID correction, remove that entire bullet; Learn explicitly documents local authentication governance as preview.

claims.claim: Specific Microsoft Purview auditing coverage for this authentication-governance control remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance Purview audit. Opened external-auth-control and View Power Pages activity logs in Microsoft Purview in full. The activity table documents other governance events but no authentication-governance event.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn already documents authentication-governance configuration even though the roadmap still says In development.
claims.quote:
Configure authentication governance controls

To configure authentication governance controls:

1. Sign in to the Power Platform admin center.
